content: Cefadroxil is a cephalosporin antibiotic that is prescribed to treat bacterial infections, including those affecting the skin, throat, and urinary tract. It is not effective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Cefadroxil is available in capsule, tablet, and liquid forms, and it is taken orally. It is typically administered once daily or every 12 hours (twice daily) for a duration of 7 to 10 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the capsules and tablets whole with a full glass of water. Even if you feel better, continue taking the medication for the full prescribed course. Do not stop taking cefadroxil without consulting your doctor. Before starting cefadroxil, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to cefadroxil, other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cefaclor or cephalexin), penicillin, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants like warfarin, probenecid, or vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, colitis, or stomach problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking cefadroxil, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking cefadroxil. Cefadroxil may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Cefadroxil may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, unusual bleeding or bruising, sore throat, painful mouth or throat sores, and vaginal infections. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store cefadroxil in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Capsules and tablets should be kept at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store in the bathroom). Liquid cefadroxil should be refrigerated and discarded after 14 days. Do not freeze the liquid form. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal of unused medication. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any required laboratory tests. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to cefadroxil. If you are diabetic, use Clinistix or TesTape to test your urine for sugar, as cefadroxil may interfere with Clinitest results. Do not share this medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of cefadroxil, contact your doctor. Cefadroxil is sold under the brand name Duricef®.
